minutes.headline: Commission denied a deck at 47 Cliff View Terrace but approved only the dock; Sunset Lane and Fire Road matters were continued.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission handled several wetlands hearings by Zoom. It approved a negative determination for a dock only at 47 Cliff View Terrace, continued the McGearn Fire Road 16 hearing to April 21 over a split roll call, and continued the Tremblay Sunset Lane notice of intent. It then held a workshop on land use regulations (firearm hunting, hours, fires and alcohol), which produced straw polls but no final votes, and began a Q&A document for the public hearing.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the opening; none raised.
A chat participant asked about a hearing at 210 Arbor Street; the chair said it was not on the agenda and awaiting DEP information.

decisions.decision: Applicant at 47 Cliff View Terrace agreed to amend the request to a dock only and return later with a broader plan.
Tremblay (386 Sunset Lane) asked for a continuance to secure a written agreement with the abutter before approval.
Applicant consented to the continuance; will request further continuance if a full board is not expected on April 21.
Straw polls kept the draft regulations: hunting at two town forests, 24-hour hours, ban on possession of firearms unless exempted, and open fires, smoking and alcohol prohibited.
Business permit form to be reviewed by the commission and the administrator to check for insurance language.
The ATV wetland incident is to be removed from the agenda and the owner sent a letter.

what_happened.line: The Commission approved a negative determination for a dock only at 47 Cliff View Terrace, after the applicant amended the request and said a broader plan would follow.
The hearing for the McGearn single-family home at 238 Fire Road 16 was continued to April 21 on a split roll call, with the applicant's consent.
The Tremblay hearing at 386 Sunset Lane was continued to April 21 so the applicant could get a written agreement with an abutter.
In a workshop on land use regulations, straw polls kept the draft rules on hunting, hours, firearms, open fires, smoking and alcohol; no final votes were taken.
A negative determination was approved for a deck replacement and three-season porch at 586 Reservoir Road.

why_it_matters: Owners with work near wetlands, such as the Fire Road 16 and Sunset Lane projects, still have no final decision, and the continued hearings can change what gets built.
The draft land use regulations would set rules for hunting, firearms, fires and alcohol on town land, and they are still unadopted, so a public hearing is the next point where residents can weigh in.
watch_next: Continued hearings for Fire Road 16 (McGearn), Sunset Lane (Tremblay), Flynn Road and Peninsula Drive return on April 21; others are set for May 5.
The draft land use regulations and their Q&A document go to a public hearing. The minutes give no date for it.
